                "LOSTag": "B.3 Forecasting techniques",
                "Difficulty": "Moderate-Easy",
                "ItemType": "MCQ",
                "ItemStyle": "single-select",
                "Stem": "Crescent observes a consistent upward pattern in monthly demand. Which response is most appropriate?",
                "Choices": {
                        "A": "Use a time-series technique that incorporates trend rather than a simple average that lags the pattern",
                        "B": "Treat the trend as a capital lease",
                        "C": "Use only a static budget variance",
                        "D": "Use the direct method of service allocation"
                },
                "CorrectChoice": "A",
                "ExplanationCorrect": "Trend-aware time-series methods are more appropriate when demand systematically increases or decreases.",
                "StudyLinks": [

                "ExplanationWrongB": "A capital lease is a financing classification under GAAP governing long-term asset acquisition, not a forecasting concept. An upward demand trend requires a time-series forecasting technique that explicitly models trend, such as trend-adjusted exponential smoothing or regression with a time variable, to avoid systematic forecast lag.",
                "ExplanationWrongC": "A static budget variance compares actual results to the original budget at planned volume — it is a performance evaluation tool, not a forecasting method.                 "ExplanationWrongD": "The direct method of service allocation is a cost accounting technique for distributing service department costs to operating departments.
